record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: For low-regularity Lorentzian metrics, such as continuous or Holder-continuous metrics for which length-maximizing timelike curves exist, is a maximizing geodesic unique; what physical interpretation should be given to non-uniqueness of the geodesic initial value problem; and should such a metric be regarded as singular?

evidence.quote: However, length maximising timelike curves will exist if the metric is merely co, and these will be o,a (O<a.<l) if the metric is co,a. Is a maximising geodesic unique in this case? Is there a physical interpretation of non-uniqueness of the IVP? In particular, should a metric for which uniqueness fails for the IVP for timelike geodesics, be considered singular?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a Lorentzian manifold whose metric tensor $g$ has low regularity. Specifically, assume either:

(a) $g$ is continuous ($C^0$) on $M$, in which case length-maximizing causal/timelike curves between causally related points are known to exist (under standard global causality assumptions); or

(b) $g$ is Hölder continuous of class $C^{0,\alpha}$ for some $0 < \alpha < 1$, in which case length-maximizing timelike curves exist and admit a $C^{1,\alpha}$ parametrization.

Consider the following questions:

1. Under hypotheses (a) or (b), is a length-maximizing timelike geodesic between two timelike-related points $p, q \in M$ necessarily unique?

2. If uniqueness can fail for the initial value problem for timelike geodesics (i.e., there exist two distinct timelike geodesics with the same initial point and initial timelike tangent vector), what physical interpretation, in the context of general relativity, should be ascribed to such non-uniqueness?

3. Should a Lorentzian metric $g$ for which uniqueness of the initial value problem for timelike geodesics fails be classified as singular?

Provide a rigorous analysis answering (1) and a principled framework addressing (2) and (3).
artifact.status_search_result: There has been substantial recent progress on geodesics for low-regularity Lorentzian metrics: existence and regularity results for length maximizers in $C^0$ and $C^{0,\alpha}$ metrics are established, and the initial value problem has been studied (e.g., Filippov-type solutions for locally Lipschitz metrics). Non-uniqueness phenomena, including counterexamples to uniqueness at Hölder regularity, are known. However, the conceptual/physical questions about the meaning of non-uniqueness and whether such metrics should be classified as singular remain only partially addressed, with active work on inextendibility and weak singularities.

status_evidence.title: On geodesics in low regularity
status_evidence.snippet: Considers geodesics in Lorentzian manifolds with metrics of low regularity, existence of extremal curves for continuous metrics, and the initial value problem for locally Lipschitz metrics.
status_evidence.claim: Existence, regularity, and uniqueness results for the geodesic IVP at low regularity have been developed.

status_evidence.title: Uniqueness and Non-Uniqueness Results for Spacetime Extensions
status_evidence.snippet: Local uniqueness fails in general for anchored extensions which are only Hölder continuous; counterexamples exist for any 0<α<1.
status_evidence.claim: Non-uniqueness phenomena at Hölder regularity are explicitly established.

status_evidence.title: On the uniqueness of continuous spacetime extensions in 1+1 dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on uniqueness of continuous spacetime extensions and weak null singularities.
status_evidence.claim: The interpretation of low-regularity non-uniqueness in terms of singular spacetimes is being actively investigated.
